title: Repo facts head
description: The bounded, structured facts a consuming repository owns. Rendered into the committed contributor-facing AGENTS.md head, above canonical public-common clauses. A fact qualifies ONLY if it is (1) executable by a clean fork with no Neo private infrastructure, (2) repo-specific or public-common rather than maintainer-institution policy, (3) mechanically falsifiable against the repo, and (4) required before the first safe contribution. `additionalProperties: false` is the cap made structural: an uncapped facts head becomes a second constitution by accretion, which is the failure this schema exists to prevent. The schema therefore REJECTS Memory Core / A2A identities, lane-claim rules, maintainer rotation, private paths, and any clause whose consumer requires a Neo seat — there is simply no property to put them in.

repository.description: owner/name. Mechanically falsifiable against the remote.

defaultRef.description: The branch a contributor targets. neo uses `dev`; devindex uses `main` — a difference a copied constitution silently omitted, which is exactly why this is a fact and not prose.

ticketAuthority.description: Where work is tracked. `none` is a legitimate answer and must be stated rather than left absent.

install.description: The exact install command a clean fork runs. No Neo private infrastructure may be required to execute it.

commands.description: Canonical invocations. Bounded deliberately: a free-form command map is prose wearing a schema.

forbiddenCommands.description: Generic invocations that LOOK correct and are wrong here. Naming them is load-bearing: `npx playwright test` runs without the project config and is the standing example — a contributor cannot infer this from a passing-looking command.

notes.description: Escape hatch, hard-capped. Three entries of 200 characters each is not enough room for a policy document — that is the point. If a required fact does not fit the properties above, the schema is incomplete and should be amended rather than absorbed here as prose.
